description:
## Problem
#4331 (head 41bc621c84) adds breach attribution, a longer admission hold, engine memory caps, a refusal of default DuckDB and Spark runs under a small budget, and kill-and-replay. The owner did not approve the caps or the refusal, evidence for them is one Spark measurement and none for DuckDB, and replay is not the pause the owner chose on 2026-11-17.

## Owner decision
"keep only breach attribution and the longer admission hold. Remove the engine caps, the default-run refusal and the replay." Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20.

## Change
On the #4331 branch, with new commits and no history rewrite: remove the engine memory caps (benchbox/utils/engine_memory.py and its callers in platform_config, the MCP benchmark tool and adapters), the default-run refusal, and the retry and replay path with its flags and docs. Keep the attribution report and the admission hold. Then repair the findings that still apply: (a) `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT_HOLD_SECONDS` accepts `inf` and loops holding the lock; (b) other sessions' command lines are logged unredacted; (c) containers the holder starts are reported as foreign memory, which makes the attribution wrong; (d) docs/agent/heavy-work.md statements that no longer match. Findings about the memory limit recorded in results, retry bounds and the retry test fall away with the removed code; confirm each is gone. Merge develop normally. Retitle the pull request and rewrite its body to what it now does.

## Decision gates
The upper bound for the hold seconds is shown to the owner before commit; until then the code refuses only non-finite and negative values. How holder-started containers are attributed is policy: if it needs more than labelling them as unknown-origin, stop and show the design. The watchdog's kill behaviour does not change. Member item heavy-guard-watchdog-20261030-deferral-1 (graceful engine failure before the watchdog) is not met by this pull request; say so on the umbrella and leave it open.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the diff against develop contains no engine cap, no refusal and no retry code or flag; a default DuckDB run under `make heavy-run` with a small budget starts as it does on develop (test); a non-finite hold value is refused (test); attribution output redacts command lines (test); the doc matches the code; `make pr-preflight` exits 0 on the pushed head; the pull request body cites only what was run.

## Guardrails (accepted by the owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, resolves a review thread, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
